newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. agency, firms eyeing Mexico power plant.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency, firms eyeing Mexico power plant.

text.p: International Energy Partners (IEP) Global Development said on Thursday it and the U.S. Trade and Development Agency began a study on the possible development of a Mexican power plant.
The planned 120 megawatt gas-fired cogeneration plant would provide steam and power to the Toluca-Lerma industrial zone, 60 miles (40 km) east of Mexico City.

"The announcement was made at a signing ceremony held at the U.S. embassy in Mexico City, at which representatives of the industrial power customers in the Toluca industrial zone and a U.S. government representative signed a cost-sharing agreement," the IEP statement said.

In the agreement, the U.S. agency would share the cost of the project feasibility study with IEP Global Development, a recently formed partnership composed of International Energy Partners and Gramercy Development Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Consolidated Edison of New York.
Companies in the industrial zone -- Chrysler Corp, Gates and Barcel -- hired IEP to carry out the study and implement the project if deemed feasible, the statement said.

"IEP has been committed to entering the power and cogeneration market in Mexico for three years. For a short while those plans were delayed, but we have always believed that there is a substantial market for economically priced, efficient power among major industrial users," IEP senior vice president Manuel Rojas said.

Mexico is inviting private companies to build new power plants, as part of efforts to boost the nation's power supply and decentralize electricity control from the government's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE).
